gallery.description: A Nottingham City Transport bus in Carrington Street in the English city of Nottingham. The bus is passing the railway station, with its clock tower, and is a Scania N94UD with East Lancs OmniDekka body, registration mark YN55 NGF, fleet number 692, in blue and silver GO2 Navy Line livery branded for route 4.

gallery.title: File:Canal House Wharf, Nottingham - geograph.org.uk - 4158256.jpg
gallery.description: Two old canal-side buildings that are now pubs in the English city of Nottingham. The building to the right is the back of what was the offices of the canal carriers Fellows Morton and Clayton, the front of which now houses a pub that goes by that name. The building with the prominent Fellows Morton and Clayton name painted on it was their warehouse, and now houses a pub called the Canal House. The two narrowboats 'Megan' and 'Tinkers Leen' are part of the Nottingham Narrowboat Project and are seen here moored at their home base.
